name: charcha
description: Self-hosted comments for static sites. Deploys to your own Cloudflare account.
author: Mayank Gupta

scripts.deploy: wrangler d1 migrations apply DB --remote && wrangler deploy
scripts.typecheck: tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json && tsc --noEmit -p src/embed/tsconfig.json && tsc --noEmit -p src/dashboard/tsconfig.json && tsc --noEmit -p test/tsconfig.json && tsc --noEmit -p test/dom/tsconfig.json && tsc --noEmit -p test/dashboard/tsconfig.json
scripts.check: pnpm types:check && pnpm typecheck && pnpm lint && pnpm format:check && pnpm test && pnpm build && pnpm check:size && pnpm check:lockfile && pnpm check:licences && pnpm check:actions && pnpm check:deploy && pnpm check:audit

CHARCHA_DASHBOARD_PASSWORD.description: **Required, and at least 15 characters — this is the only credential for your moderation dashboard and it has no second factor.** Generate one with `openssl rand -base64 24`, which gives you 32, and keep it in a password manager: there is no account to create, no second user and no reset, and anyone holding it can approve, hide and delete every comment on your site. Nothing on this form will check the length — it cannot — so it is worth pasting a generated value rather than typing one; the dashboard's Setup tab will tell you later if this one was short, and [the README](https://github.com/withsetu/charcha#how-long-the-dashboard-password-should-be) says why nothing ever refuses it. Left empty, the dashboard refuses every request including its own login, and comments arriving on your site cannot be moderated. Turnstile, email notifications and the rest are **not** asked for here — they are off until you switch them on afterwards, and the [README](https://github.com/withsetu/charcha#turning-on-the-optional-features) has the one command each. The bot check is the one of those worth doing; the field below says why it is not on this form.

IP_HASH_SECRET.description: **Required, and any long random string will do — `openssl rand -hex 32` if you have a terminal open.** This is the key that turns a commenter's IP address into the identifier the per-IP spam rate limit counts. It is an HMAC key, not a credential to look up anywhere: nothing has to recognise it, it never leaves your Worker, and no IP address is stored without it. Use a random one — anyone who guessed it and also had a copy of your database could turn the stored hashes back into IP addresses. **One spam layer is not on this form, and it is the strongest one: [Turnstile](https://developers.cloudflare.com/turnstile/get-started/).** Every other layer measures the absence of something wrong; Turnstile is the only one that asks a commenter's browser to prove itself, and Cloudflare's free plan is unlimited. It is missing here because this form requires a value in every field, and a Turnstile secret invented to get past a required field matches no widget — which would hold every comment on your site for review. So turn it on after deploying, and turn on **both** of a widget's keys: the secret key goes on the Worker and the sitekey goes on your own page as `data-turnstile-sitekey`. [The README](https://github.com/withsetu/charcha#turning-on-the-optional-features) has both steps.
